# Psalm 137 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 137:5 (overlap: 7%)

- **EMET:** If I-forget-you O-Jerusalem, let-forget my-right-hand.
- **LOGOS:** If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill!
- **PNEUMA:** If I ever forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand lose all its skill.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 137:8 (overlap: 7%)

- **EMET:** O-daughter-of Babylon the-devastated; blessed the-one-who repays to-you your-dealing which you-dealt to-us.
- **LOGOS:** O daughter of Babylon, doomed to be destroyed, blessed shall he be who repays you with what you have done to us!
- **PNEUMA:** Babylon, you destroyer — a blessing on whoever pays you back for what you did to us!

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 137:9 (overlap: 8%)

- **EMET:** Blessed the-one-who seizes and-dashes your-infants against the-rock.
- **LOGOS:** Blessed shall he be who takes your little ones and dashes them against the rock!
- **PNEUMA:** A blessing on whoever grabs your babies and smashes them against the rocks!

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 137:4 (overlap: 8%)

- **EMET:** How shall-we-sing song-of YHWH on soil-of foreignness?
- **LOGOS:** How shall we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?
- **PNEUMA:** But how can we sing the LORD's song in a foreign country?

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 137:2 (overlap: 11%)

- **EMET:** On willows in-her-midst we-hung our-lyres.
- **LOGOS:** On the willows there we hung up our lyres.
- **PNEUMA:** We hung our harps on the willow trees nearby.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 137:6 (overlap: 11%)

- **EMET:** Let-cling my-tongue to-my-palate if not I-remember-you, if not I-raise Jerusalem above the-head-of my-joy.
- **LOGOS:** Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth, if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy!
- **PNEUMA:** Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I don't remember you — if I don't consider Jerusalem my greatest joy.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
